summary: Susan Meinheit is a Tibetologist who held posts at the Library of Congress (attested in 1998 and 2007).

Sinologist and historian Susan Naquin earned a BA from Stanford University (~1962–1966) and an MA and PhD from Yale University (~1966–1974). She served at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–1993) and as a professor at Princeton University (1993–2013).

Susan Neiman is a philosopher who studied at Harvard (PhD ~1977–1986) and the Free University of Berlin. She held professorships at Yale (1989–1996) and Tel Aviv University (1996–2000), and became Director of the Einstein Forum in 2000.
Susan Niditch is a religious studies scholar who served as a faculty member in the religion department at Amherst College from ~1978 to 2020.

Susan Whitfield, working in Central Asian studies, history, and sinology, completed her PhD at SOAS (~1990–1995). She directed the British Library's International Dunhuang Project (~1994–2017) and held posts at UCL (~2017) and the Sainsbury Institute (~2020).

Susanne Hoeber Rudolph (1930–2015) was an Indology and history scholar. She studied at Sarah Lawrence College, Harvard, and Radcliffe. She taught political science at Harvard (~1955–1963), was a professor at the University of Chicago (1964), and presided over APSA (2003–2004).

Susanne Mrozik is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned an MTS at Harvard, supervised by Charles Hallisey. She held academic posts at Western Michigan University (attested 2002) and Mount Holyoke College (attested 2009).

Sushanta Sen worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Visva-Bharati University, where he became a lecturer in 1986, and served as a lecturer in Indian religions in the Department of Theology at the University of Birmingham.

Indologist Sushil Kumar De studied at Presidency College, Calcutta, SOAS, and Bonn. He taught English at Presidency and Calcutta (~1913–1923), was professor of Sanskrit and Bengali at Dhaka (~1923–1947), and led Jadavpur's Bengali department from 1947.
Susmita Basu Majumdar, working in history, archaeology, and Indology, was educated at Lady Brabourne College and the University of Calcutta, where she held an academic post around 2004.

Buddhist studies and sinology scholar Susumu Otake studied at the University of Tsukuba under Makio Takemura (~1993–2002). He served as a part-time lecturer at Hanazono University (~2008), Kyoto University (~2008), and Bukkyo University (~2012).

Susumu Shimazono studied at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley. He served as professor of religious studies at the University of Tokyo (1995–2013), later holding posts at Sophia University (~2013–2018) and directing its Grief Care Institute (~2017–2021).

Susumu Yamaguchi (1895–1976) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Otani, Paris, and Kyoto, under Lévi, Sasaki, Teramoto, and La Vallée Poussin. He was a professor at Otani (1934–1964) and Kyoto Sangyo (1964).

Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri studied at London, Pennsylvania, and Toronto. He founded the Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies, serving as its president (~2000), and held posts at the University of Toronto (attested 2001) and Ontario Tech University.

Suzanne Karpelès studied at the EPHE under Lévi, Foucher, and Finot. She served at EFEO (1922–1925), was the first curator of the National Library of Cambodia (1925), and became the Buddhist Institute's first secretary-general (1930).

Suzanne Newcombe earned a doctorate from Cambridge (attested 2008). Working in religious studies and Indology, she held positions at LSE, Cambridge, Inform (attested 2008, 2020), and as senior lecturer at Open University (attested 2020).

Sven Hedin (1865–1952) was a Central Asian and Tibetan studies explorer and scholar. He studied at Stockholm University, Uppsala University, the Humboldt University of Berlin under Ferdinand von Richthofen (~1889–1892), and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1892).
Sven Sellmer is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and computational methods who has held academic posts at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf and Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań.
Sven Wittemann is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

Swami Lakshman Joo (1907–1991), working in Indology and philosophy, studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan (1926–1933). He founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991 and taught scholars including Lilian Silburn, André Padoux, and Alexis Sanderson.
